4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Our delegation arrived at Holsord International Airport early in the afternoon. President Ewald Alphonso and a contingent of Sordish officials were there to greet us.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: By the time we reached the base of Holsord Tower, the sun had begun to dip lower in the sky, bathing the city in a golden hue.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: My councilor Laurento Esquibel accompanied me, as did Vina.
6.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true)

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: As our vehicle came to a stop, President Alphonso stepped forward with a welcoming gesture.

9.speaker: Player_Romus
9.text: "Both of our nations have little time to waste. Let's go ahead."

10.speaker: Player_Romus
10.text: "President Alphonso. What a grand venue for our equally grand designs."

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "The success of our whiskey-wine deal and resort investment has paved a solid path for us. I'm excited to continue on this trajectory."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "Our successful whiskey-wine trade deal has certainly set a positive tone. Today, we have the opportunity to continue on that trajectory."
20.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true)

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "I regret that we couldn't come to an agreement the last time we met. But today's meeting opens new doors for potential collaboration."
21.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true) == false)

22.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
22.text: "As am I, your Majesty. You'll be glad to know that Sordland's opinion of Rizia has risen considerably since those deals were made."

23.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
23.text: "Good to hear. The new Sordland values the prospect of working closely with Rizia, and we're hopeful that this visit will be a turning point."

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: Accompanying me were my councilors Laurento Esquibel and Elena Werner.
30.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false)

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Accompanying me were my councilors Laurento Esquibel and Elena Werner, as well as my daughter.

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: Accompanying me were my key advisors, including Laurento Esquibel.
38.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false)

41.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
41.text: "Consider us at your service, Your Highness. Should you have any requests or need assistance, please don't hesitate to let me know."

48.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
48.text: "I can't tell you how much I've been looking forward to today. It's an occasion to celebrate the multi-faceted economic partnership we are building between our great nations."

49.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
49.text: "It stands as a symbol of the aspirations of the Sordish people. Including my own aspirations to further the economic partnership we've begun to build between our two great nations."
49.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true)

50.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
50.text: "It stands as a symbol of the aspirations of the Sordish people. Including my own aspirations to achieve a win-win deal between our great nations."
50.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Sordland_WineWhiskeyDeal"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Economy_Sordland_ResortDeal"] == true) == false)

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: Upon entering the grand lobby of Holsord Tower, we were directed towards a lavish elevator.

52.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
52.text: "Holsord's modernity represents our drive towards progress, much like our efforts in modernizing Sordland's key industries."

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: The cabin slowly ascended, giving us a momentary sense of detachment from the world below. The cityscape of Holsord became a moving panorama through the glass walls.

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "We're certainly not in Porte Drazon anymore."

55.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
55.text: "Quite the sight, isn't it? It's always interesting to see Holsord from this perspective. I hope your first impression of our city is a favorable one."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "I'll admit I'm impressed. But I've always believed that the true character of a city is found not in its skyline but in the lives of its people."

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: A server came around and poured us glasses of a cloudy-looking liquid that I recognized as kebij. It was time for me to make the opening remarks for the bond deal discussion.

58.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
58.text: "Right on. It's the everyday folks that really tell you what a place is about, recession or not."

59.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
59.text: "You can't just cling to the past if you want to move forward. But then, forgetting where you came from isn't the answer either."

60.speaker: Elena Werner
60.text: "The true test of a city is how it supports its most vulnerable. Especially during times of economic instability, wouldn't you say, Mr. President?"

61.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
61.text: "We understand completely. Rizia is in the process of evolving right now, while holding on to what makes us unique as a nation."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "I'm much more interested in seeing the Maroon Palace later. Concrete needles don't impress me as much as history and culture."

63.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
63.text: "I should have expected you'd be a history buff. The Maroon Palace does hold stories that no modern edifice can."

64.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
64.text: "Direct and to the point – a quality I admire. Time is indeed a luxury we don't have in abundance."

65.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
65.text: "We'll continue this conversation over dinner. The views from the revolving restaurant are nothing less than astounding."

68.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
68.text: "As the tower defies the limits of architecture, so too can our nations push the limits of partnership."

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: A silence settled between the delegations.

78.speaker: Player_Romus
78.text: "You know, this could be good training for your upcoming elections against Anton Rayne. A nod-off, perhaps?"

80.speaker: Player_Romus
80.text: "Is this a Sordish tradition, President Alphonso?"

81.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
81.text: "Why do you think Sordish necks are this thick? All the diplomatic nodding we do."

82.speaker: Player_Romus
82.text: "I'm beginning to think I should allocate a separate budget for neck massages."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "Maybe we should start a new trend – diplomatic winks instead. It’s less strenuous and twice as mysterious!"

84.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
84.text: "Princess Vina, it's an honor to welcome you. Mr. Manger and our team will ensure all your needs are met during your stay."

88.speaker: Vina Toras
88.text: "Thank you, President Alphonso. I've studied much about Sordland's recent history and can't wait to experience its culture first-hand."

89.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
89.text: "I suspect this is an unspoken contest of diplomatic resilience. Let's call it a draw for now and save our strength for the discussions ahead."

90.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
90.text: "At this rate, we'll need to train our diplomats not just in etiquette, but in endurance. Perhaps Sordland can lead the way in nodding diplomacy."

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "Why, thank you. It's comforting to know Princess Vina will be in good hands."

92.speaker: Player_Romus
92.text: "You'll be the one begging for assistance after a few hours of my daughter asking questions."

93.speaker: Player_Romus
93.text: "Splendid. And if today's meeting goes like our last did, I assume a taste of Sordland's finest beverages is in order."

94.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
94.text: "If Your Majesty desires, so it will be. Although you've already made it abundantly clear what you think of our whiskey--"

95.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
95.text: "Ha. Ask away, Your Highness! You're talking to an expert."

96.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
96.text: "No worries, Your Majesty. We'll make sure your entire delegation gets the full Sordish experience – top-notch and no fuss."

97.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
97.text: "We appreciate it, Mr. Manger. It's important for us to see Sordland the way it truly is, beyond the official veneer."

98.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
98.text: "Just don't tire them out too much, Vina. We still need them focused for our meetings."

99.speaker: Vina Toras
99.text: "Yes, please don't feel the need to put on a show on my behalf."

100.speaker: Vina Toras
100.text: "Don't worry. There are a great many things I'm curious about, though."

101.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
101.text: "If it's beverages you want, we'll introduce you to kebij. I warn you that it's a bit... rustic, but it has its own special charms."

102.speaker: Player_Romus
102.text: "Just wait until you try Sordish zabla, Vina. It's the best."

103.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
103.text: "You know our cuisine well, Your Majesty! Yes, nothing beats zabla with a cold glass of kebij... or Erlory Maroon."

104.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
104.text: "But you've already made it clear what Rizia thinks of our fine whiskey, haven't you?"

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: Alphonso shot him a warning look. He shut his mouth.

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: "As long as you avoid any overly rowdy or scandalous activities that might not befit her status as a princess."

107.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
107.text: "Understood, Your Majesty. We'll make sure all events are up to royal standards – sophisticated, respectful, absolutely dripping with taste."

108.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
108.text: "We Rizians cut loose every now and again too, you know. But we do wish to refrain from making too much of a stir abroad."

109.speaker: Vina Toras
109.text: "I can handle a little rowdiness, Father. I find it charming in its own way."

112.speaker: Player_Romus
112.text: "At this rate, I'm considering incorporating nodding into our national fitness program."

113.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
113.text: "Diplomatic winks, now that's an innovation! But imagine the misunderstandings – we might need a whole new protocol for that."

114.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
114.text: "A national fitness trend based on diplomacy – now there’s a novel idea. It would certainly make international relations a bit more... physically engaging."

115.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
115.text: "Ahem. Glad as I am to see you both in agreement, shall we move on to more pressing matters?"

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: He nodded back again and shook my hand even harder.

119.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
119.text: "Are we setting a new standard for international greetings?"

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: "Only if the next standard involves a friendly arm-wrestling match, President Alphonso. It could be the ultimate test of diplomatic strength!"

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "Perhaps but I'm holding out for the day when we switch to high-fives. It’s the future of international relations!"

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "I was thinking more along the lines of a staring contest. First one to blink handles the next trade negotiation!"

123.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
123.text: "An arm-wrestling match? Now that would be a sight at the next AN summit. I’ll start training right away to beat Chairman Hegel!"

124.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
124.text: "High-fives could indeed add some flair to our meetings."

125.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
125.text: "Well, King Romus, this must be a record for the longest handshake in diplomatic history!"

126.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
126.text: "As much as I'd enjoy seeing these new diplomatic practices, perhaps we should reserve our strength for the negotiations ahead."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: President Ewald Alphonso's gaze briefly swept across our group before settling on Princess Vina.

128.speaker: Player_Romus
128.text: "Oh, it is. A perfect blend of history and modernity, just as we're striving to achieve in Rizia."

129.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
129.text: "Yeah, it's something. But remember, we used to be a kingdom too. Beneath all this modernity, we've still got our historical roots."

130.speaker: Elena Werner
130.text: "One does wonder how your country's recession has affected the lives behind these modern facades."

131.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
131.text: "I promise you that once the market readjusts itself, Holsord's citizens will reap the fruits of our privatization initiatives. The streets will come alive once more."

132.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
132.text: "Unlike a certain Colonel Soll, I and my administration have no intention of erasing Sordland's history."

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: From the cobbled streets of the Old Town to the skyscrapers of the Maroon District, the greenery of the Capitol Park to the diversity of New Erlory – the city was a seamless blend of past and present.

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "President Alphonso, could you tell us more about the Old Town?"

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "I would love to learn more about Holsord, Mr. President."

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "I believe our time would be better spent discussing the future of our bilateral relations."

147.speaker: Player_Romus
147.text: "What inspired the development of the Maroon District? It's quite a contrast to the Old Town."

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "Capitol Park and the surrounding government buildings are impressive."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "Is that a street market I see down in New Erlory?"

154.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
154.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_OldTownListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_MaroonDistrictListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_CapitolParkGovDistrictListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_NewErloryListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_EvolutionListened"] == true

155.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
155.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_OldTownListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_MaroonDistrictListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_CapitolParkGovDistrictListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_NewErloryListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_EvolutionListened"] == true) == false

156.speaker: Player_Romus
156.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_OldTownListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_MaroonDistrictListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_CapitolParkGovDistrictListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_NewErloryListened"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_EvolutionListened"] == true

157.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
157.text: "It's a lot like your Old Town in Porte Drazon, just... newer. The city was founded on the east side of the Eskel River in the early 1400s. It started as a key rest and recovery stop for traders, growing significantly during the Renan period."

158.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
158.text: "Its architecture, from the Renan days to the Sordish-Agnolian union-state era, is a mirror of Sordland's history."

159.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
159.text: "That's right. The Old Town's got this timeless aura, you know? The tourists can't get enough of it."

160.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
160.text: "It's got all the fancy buildings, businesses, embassies... everything a modern metropolis could need."

161.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
161.text: "Its blend of modernist and neo-classical architecture reflected the aspirations Soll held for a progressive Sordland. At the time."

162.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
162.text: "That's what our late President Wisci intended. His initial conception for the district was taken over by President Tarquin Soll after the Civil War. It was renamed to symbolize the rebirth of Holsord under the Second Republic."

163.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
163.text: "The park's a favorite spot for folks around here. Great place to relax and get away from the city rush."

164.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
164.text: "And the government buildings, including the Maroon Palace and the Grand National Assembly, are not just architectural marvels but also the epicenters of our nation's governance."

165.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
165.text: "These buildings represent our democratic journey, especially the Assembly where elected representatives work for Sordland's future."

166.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
166.text: "Yes, it's there every week. Part of the district's melting-pot charm."

167.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
167.text: "Ever since migrants from Erlory started settling there a century ago, it's attracted all kinds of diverse inhabitants. I'd call it Holsord's most vibrant neighborhood."

168.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
168.text: "Not to mention that the nightlife can't be beat. Remind me to take you to Cabaret Lachaven if we have time after dinner."

172.speaker: Player_Romus
172.text: "How do you see the evolution of Holsord?"

173.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
173.text: "I'd say it mirrors that of Sordland itself. It's been rebuilding, growing, changing with the times."

174.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
174.text: "And just like Sordland, it stands strong no matter what's thrown at it."

175.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
175.text: "Even in the face of our recent... challenges."

176.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
176.text: "You read the news, Your Majesty. I won't pretend the Sordish economy hasn't seen a downturn since our last meeting."

180.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
180.text: "I have to say, such swift policy changes would be much easier to implement in a monarchy like yours. You have no idea how much bureaucracy and obstruction we've been facing."

181.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
181.text: "The Rizian government does have checks and balances, Mr. President. But yes, such bureaucratic hurdles are practically unheard of under our system."

182.speaker: Vina Toras
182.text: "I understand completely, Mr. President. But if I may be so bold, how can you be sure these radical changes won't deepen the divide between the rich and poor in your country?"

183.speaker: Elena Werner
183.text: "The challenge, then, is ensuring these reforms don't disproportionately affect the less privileged."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "You may have heard we're striving to diversify Rizia's economy away from resources. Holsord's modernity is an inspiration to us."

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "I can't help but admire the strategic planning that went into Holsord's development."

198.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
198.text: "Yes, well, the challenge lies in ensuring this development reaches all layers of society. It's a delicate task, especially in these trying economic times."

199.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
199.text: "The drive for progress sometimes overshadows the needs of the common folk. In Rizia, we try our best to not rattle any feathers."

203.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
203.text: "Yes, it's been quite the challenge to explore new economic paths while staying true to our historic roots."

204.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
204.text: "Valgen, the place where I'm from, has been struggling to do the very same thing. It's difficult, but it's the only way to survive."

205.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
205.text: "The reforms we have embarked on in the last five years is the medicine our economy needed for the long-term future. It may take a while, but we'll get out of Soll's stagnation."

209.speaker: Vina Toras
209.text: "Which is not to say that we reject the idea of change entirely, President Alphonso. We're doing our best to bring the monarchy in line with the needs of the present."

213.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
213.text: "All progress comes with some sacrifice. Our people will be better off in the long-term."

214.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
214.text: "But the recession of '51 was a direct result of the entrenched systemic issues we inherited. Thanks to the aggressive economic reforms I'm putting into place, our growth will only skyrocket from here."

215.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
215.text: "It may be a controversial move, but privatizing key sectors -- and, crucially, attracting foreign investment -- will position Sordland towards a globally competitive, prosperous and stable future in the 60s."

216.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
216.text: "I'm almost jealous. It's been a real pain trying to explain economic growth to our more thick-headed Assembly members."

217.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
217.text: "Just imagine, Ewald. If Sordland were a monarchy again, we'd be able to push these reforms in the blink of an eye."

218.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
218.text: "As someone who's worked in rural areas and seen the reality, let me tell you – investment and growth often lift all boats."

219.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
219.text: "Sure, we need to tackle the wealth gap. But it's not just about handouts; it's about creating real, sustainable opportunities."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "I appreciate what you've done for your country. But in Rizia, we prefer gradual changes. Tradition must always be respected."

221.speaker: Player_Romus
221.text: "Such aggressive reforms may work in Sordland. But in Rizia, sudden changes have the potential to unsettle the populace to a dangerous degree."

222.speaker: Player_Romus
222.text: "I see the merit in your approach. Rizia itself could benefit from the kind of liberal economic changes you're implementing here."

223.speaker: Player_Romus
223.text: "I'm completely on board with your approach. Rizia itself is undergoing a series of privatization measures."

224.speaker: Narrator
224.text: The staff guided us towards a large table. The gentle hum of conversation enveloped us as we were seated.

226.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
226.text: "So I've heard! It's encouraging to know that beneath those kingly robes beats the heart of a fellow fiscal liberal."

227.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
227.text: "It's encouraging to hear that you see the potential in liberal reforms, Your Majesty. Just as I acknowledge the benefits of Rizia's adherence to tradition."

228.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
228.text: "Undoubtedly, the pace of reform must match society's readiness for change."

229.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
229.text: "Rapid reforms do come with risks. However, we in Sordland reached a point where the risk of inaction outweighed the risk of change."

230.speaker: Player_Romus
230.text: "We do cherish our monarchy in Rizia. But we're also open to learning from the reform experiences of nations like Sordland."

231.speaker: Player_Romus
231.text: "You're overestimating how easy it is to pass reforms in Rizia. The public doesn't react well to sudden changes of any kind."

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "Our methods may differ. But in the end, both of us share the common goal of bettering our citizens' lives."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "I daresay you'd look good with a crown on your head, Mr. President."

235.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
235.text: "Great to know, Your Majesty. It sounds like our countries still have much to learn from each other."

237.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
237.text: "Any questions about this magnificent panorama, Your Majesty? I'm happy to offer my insights into the various districts of our fair city."

238.speaker: Narrator
238.text: The elevator gently halted at the top of Holsord Tower and the doors slid open, revealing the entrance to the revolving restaurant. Alphonso continued to talk.

245.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
245.text: "But ultimately, I do rest easier knowing that the most important government decisions in Sordland are not mine to make alone."

246.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
246.text: "It's proof that our countries have much to offer each other."

247.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
247.text: "The Sordish people elected me precisely because I promised them change. And I aim to bring it to them."

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: The restaurant's large windows offered an unobstructed view of Holsord's expanse.

257.speaker: Player_Romus
257.text: "So would you say Gasom played a role in shaping modern Sordland?"

258.speaker: Player_Romus
258.text: "Monarchist sentiments, right. I admit I'm interested in the role of General Eduard Luderin and the Black Battalion after the Sordish monarchy fell."

259.speaker: Player_Romus
259.text: "Tell me more about the Restoration Period."

260.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
260.text: "You know that I started out at Gasom in the aftermath of the Civil War, during the Restoration Period."

262.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
262.text: "Gasom became a symbol of our national resurgence. I remember navigating through the maze of old monarchist sentiments and the ambitions of Soll and his new republic..."

263.speaker: Narrator
263.text: Alphonso took a sip from his whiskey and looked out into the distance.

264.speaker: Player_Romus
264.text: "I'm sure Soll's National Autarky Plan posed difficulties for you as a businessman."

265.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
265.text: "Not to be immodest, but yes. Under my leadership, Gasom transitioned from a state-controlled entity to a key player in the global energy market."

266.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
266.text: "Ah, yes. That particular movement was a significant counterforce during Sordland's transition to democracy. It gave us an idea of the deep-seated monarchist loyalties some Sords still had."

267.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
267.text: "Simply put, it was a time of rebuilding and reimagining Sordland's future."

268.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
268.text: "It wasn't all bad. You'll recall my predecessor's original intent with the NAP was to make Sordland self-sufficient and independent from foreign influences."

269.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
269.text: "Let's not bore our delegation further. We all know why you're really here."

270.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
270.text: "Today the corporation stands as a symbol of our success in attracting foreign investment and technological advancement. Proving Sordland's resilience and adaptability in a changing world economy."

271.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
271.text: "Ultimately, their defeat helped solidify the republic's foundation, but it also left lingering questions about national unity and the role of traditionalist forces in modern Sordland."

272.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
272.text: "Soll's government made massive efforts to repair the war's physical and social damage, creating a new civic identity grounded in republican values."

273.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
273.text: "While it succeeded in some respects, like infrastructure development, it also isolated us economically."

274.speaker: Player_Romus
274.text: "What about your own history with Holsord, Mr. President?"
274.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_OldTownListened"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_MaroonDistrictListened"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_CapitolParkGovDistrictListened"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_NewErloryListened"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_SordlandBond_EvolutionListened"] == true

275.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
275.text: Raise your glass for a toast. [Drink.]

276.speaker: Player_Romus
276.text: "Thank you for the hospitality and kindness you've shown us thus far. I'm eager to hear your proposal."

280.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
280.text: "So. What we're offering Rizia is the chance to purchase Sordish government bonds with a four-year maturity at excellent rates."

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: There was a pause in the discussion as the first course was served. It was a deconstructed version of Lachaven-style lorscha, with a hot seafood stock poured over clams, mussels and cubed raw salmon.

282.speaker: Narrator
282.text: After we'd been eating for a few minutes, President Alphonso cleared his throat.

283.speaker: Player_Romus
283.text: "Given the current recession in Sordland, how can you assure us that these investments will bear fruit?"

284.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
284.text: "Despite the current recession, we're on a path to economic revitalization, thanks to significant investments being secured from Qinal and Anraka as well as our progressive policy reforms."

285.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
285.text: "This bond issue is a chance for Rizia not only to make financial gains, but also to diversify its economy."

289.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
289.text: "This bond issue is a chance for Rizia not only to make financial gains, but to strengthen its resource-based economy through energy investments into Sordland. We will offer discounts if we see eye to eye on this deal."

290.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
290.text: "I understand that. But with great risk comes great reward."

291.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
291.text: "We need to review the economic performance indicators and further recovery plans thoroughly. Growth forecasts alone aren't enough."

292.speaker: Elena Werner
292.text: "And risky. As we've seen from time to time with our own Rizian Royal Gold company, privatization has its drawbacks."

293.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
293.text: "A valid question. But our economic policies are designed to withstand political changes."

294.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
294.text: "As I mentioned, the investments we're received from Qinal and Anraka are substantial. Coupled with our reforms, they're projected to significantly boost our economy."

295.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
295.text: "This is not mere speculation. Our plans are calculated based on economic principles behind a sound free-market strategy."

296.speaker: Player_Romus
296.text: "Your re-election is far from guaranteed, President Alphonso. How can we be sure your successor will follow the economic course you've set?"

297.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
297.text: "The landscape in Sordland is ever-changing, and Anton Rayne could well prevail in the next elections. Despite this, the bond proposal is built with long-term stability and growth in mind."

298.speaker: Player_Romus
298.text: "You mentioned future benefits for Rizia by signing this deal. Could you elaborate on what these might entail?"

299.speaker: Player_Romus
299.text: "Aren't you concerned about how this might affect Sordland's domestic market?"

300.speaker: Player_Romus
300.text: "Can you be any more specific about how our economy will benefit?"

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "Sounds promising, but I'm concerned about your elections. How can we be sure this isn't just a fleeting partnership?"

302.speaker: Player_Romus
302.text: "Your liberal economic policies, your plan to sell shares of Gasom... it's all very ambitious."

312.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
312.text: "I'd like to move on to the financial specifics of our government bonds, focusing on the returns in Rizian Guilders."

313.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
313.text: "Based on your current treasury status, I'd suggest you go with our bigger, better proposal. Invest 12 billion Rizian guilders now, and your returns will be through the roof."

314.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
314.text: "Now, considering a more cautious investment of 3 billion Rizian Guilders, the potential returns in the case of a successful economic recovery are still impressive."

315.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
315.text: "If our projections are accurate, Rizia could see its investment grow to about 9 billion guilders. Not as much as if you'd invested more, but nothing to sneeze at either."

316.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
316.text: "Foreshadowing Sordland's broader economic pivot towards market liberalization, I may add."

317.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
317.text: "Some of those traditionalist forces evolved into the National Front Party, while others formed the conservative wing of the USP itself."

318.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
318.text: "In Holsord, this meant not only overhauling the city's infrastructure, but also its very culture. But by the '40s, many of the programs had become unnecessary."

319.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
319.text: "In the end, the result was a constrained economy, lacking in innovation and global competitiveness. That's why we stagnated in the '40s."

320.speaker: Player_Romus
320.text: "In light of our recent international tribulations, we in Rizia are eager to pursue new partnerships."

321.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
321.text: "Merkopan geopolitics can be very treacherous. Rest assured that in Sordland, you can find a safe and trusted source for the future."

322.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
322.text: "I do know that your treasury has seen a reduction in income lately. We are looking for investments for this deal and hope you can afford such endeavors."

323.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
323.text: "I do know that your treasury has been seeing a significant influx of funds lately."

324.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
324.text: "Assuming you are able to invest into Sordland, we can promise you very lucrative returns."

325.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
325.text: "Money that sits around is money wasted. Nobody wants that, not even the Golden Kingdom."

326.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
326.text: "Additionally, Rizian energy output seems to be historically low at the moment."

327.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
327.text: "It's great to see strong energy production in Rizia. We could arrange future purchases of energy from your kingdom if our relations develop."

328.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
328.text: "We can't do much about that right now, but perhaps today can be a stepping stone towards a lucrative agreement in that direction."

329.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
329.text: "Sordish industries are seeing demand that not even our own Gasom can meet."

330.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
330.text: "We're talking about a budget increase of upwards of 36 billion guilders over the bond's term. You'd be tripling your money."

331.speaker: Narrator
331.text: As the restaurant continued its gentle orbit, our second course arrived. It consisted of an airy sheep-cheese mousse between two sheets of crisp pastry, garnished with a rainbow of fresh herbs and edible flowers.

332.speaker: Narrator
332.text: Gus took a quick sip from his glass of Sordish wine.

333.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
333.text: "A larger bond investment does seem like a good way to leverage the momentum we've built."

334.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
334.text: "The question now is, where does Rizia see itself in the future? As a regional power in South Merkopa, or are you aiming for a more global presence?"

341.speaker: Vina Toras
341.text: "No matter what, we Rizians do see ourselves as an influential force. Our culture, our resources, our strategic position... all of that matters in Merkopa and beyond."

342.speaker: Elena Werner
342.text: "Here's what I think. From an economic standpoint, our goal should be balanced growth."

346.speaker: Elena Werner
346.text: "Very true, Your Highness. But diving headfirst into the global arena demands a robust economic foundation."

347.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
347.text: "Here is what I believe. In my years of diplomatic service, I've seen Rizia's influence grow. We do have the capability and resources to be more than just a regional power."

348.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
348.text: "Well said, Your Highness. Yet as a seasoned diplomat, I must emphasize prudence."

349.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
349.text: "Your caution is prudent, Ms. Werner, but I believe in the dynamism of capitalism. It thrives on bold moves and calculated risks."

350.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
350.text: "Our bond proposal is a stepping stone towards that future, where Rizia is not at the corner of global politics, but a leading voice."

351.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
351.text: "That perspective aligns with my vision of practical yet forward-thinking capitalism."

352.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
352.text: "Well said, Elena. Ideally, we should be strengthening our regional influence while gradually looking for new partners."

353.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
353.text: "Valid thoughts, Mr. Esquibel. But progressive capitalism is all about seizing opportunities and being at the forefront of economic innovation."

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "These numbers are impressive, but they hinge on a lot of 'ifs' and 'maybes.' I need more than optimistic projections to justify such a large investment."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "This could be a game-changer for Rizia's budget."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "While the prospect is appealing, I'm inclined to err on the side of caution."

358.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
358.text: "Consider the concept of 'risk diversification' in economic theory."

359.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
359.text: "Think about it, Your Majesty. If your grandmother Queen Lyza had exerted similar caution, neither of our countries would be where they are today."

360.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
360.text: "Oh, yes. By embracing the principles of free-market capitalism, we can unlock new heights of prosperity."

361.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
361.text: "Think of our shared history, and how trade prospered under Queen Lyza. It's proof of how calculated risks can lead to enduring economic booms."

362.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
362.text: "What do you say to this new opportunity, King Romus?"

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "What do you think I should do, Vina?"

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "Laurento, what are your thoughts on this bond deal?"

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "Elena, what's your final perspective on this bond deal?"

367.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
367.text: Flip a coin to decide investment.

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: Gus, a hint of amusement in his eyes, watched as the coin spun upwards, glinting in the light.

377.speaker: Player_Romus
377.text: "Forget it. Let's do the investment regardless."

378.speaker: Player_Romus
378.text: "Our limited budget is only temporary. I promise you, we'll have more money available soon."

385.speaker: Player_Romus
385.text: "It might look like we have limited energy now, but you can expect that to change in the near future."

386.speaker: Player_Romus
386.text: "I'm aware of our treasury shortcomings. My council and I are doing our best to address them."

387.speaker: Player_Romus
387.text: "I'm focused on improving the energy situation. Expect us to have a high net surplus soon."

388.speaker: Player_Romus
388.text: "You've done your research, Mr. Manger. But only I and my council know the full picture."

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "A Morgna wes core! Glovurius axa Rizia."

391.speaker: Player_Romus
391.text: "To both our nations. To our future!"

392.speaker: Player_Romus
392.text: "I want to raise this glass in honor of my daughter, Princess Vina Toras."

396.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
396.text: "The Toras family honors us with the presence of both the princess and the king."

398.speaker: Vina Toras
398.text: "The honor is mine, Father. Thank you all for the generous hospitality you've shown us thus far."

399.speaker: Narrator
399.text: The focus of both delegations shifted towards Vina.

400.speaker: Narrator
400.text: The Rizian delegation cheered and clapped. The Sordish delegation raised their drinks and had a sip.

401.speaker: Narrator
401.text: Everyone at our table cheered and clapped.

402.speaker: Narrator
402.text: The sound of both delegations' applause filled the room.

403.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
403.text: "I'll add that trade between Rizia and Sordland has grown faster than anticipated thanks to that agreement. Rizians have developed quite the taste for Erlory Maroon."

404.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
404.text: "That's great to hear, Mr. President. The deals have had quite the impact in Rizia as well."

408.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
408.text: "The resort deal coincided with our modernization of the Port of Monqiz, and the synergy has been nothing less than magical."

409.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
409.text: "According to reports from our treasurer, our alcoholic beverage industry has witnessed a doubling in commerce, accompanied by a significant uptick in consumption metrics."

413.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
413.text: "While the surge in tourism to the area hasn't quite met our highest expectations, we're still seeing substantial growth."

420.speaker: Elena Werner
420.text: "Of course, the main objective with the port was to streamline our trade processes. Which it's doing even as we speak."

421.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
421.text: "We are keen to know about the current economic situation of the Kingdom of Rizia. Our recent research and inquiries haven't been fully answered."

428.speaker: Vina Toras
428.text: "Needless to say, Mr. President, the Koronti resort has been the talk of the town among Valenqiris locals."

429.speaker: Elena Werner
429.text: "But the additional tourism revenue on top of that has been a welcome fringe benefit."

436.speaker: Elena Werner
436.text: "The tax revenue has been substantial, though not as much as it would be if our wine exports were not limited by Rizian whiskey demand."

437.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
437.text: "This boom could be a gateway to exploring new markets and diversifying our export portfolio."

438.speaker: Vina Toras
438.text: "I will say that not everyone in Rizia has been on board with the increased alcohol consumption."

439.speaker: Vina Toras
439.text: "The Golcondist community in particular has reservations."

440.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
440.text: "Exactly. This is a cornerstone of our long-term economic vision: ensuring both nations benefit from our shared growth and presence in the world market."

441.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
441.text: "We've seen potential in our own beverage sector as well. But it's essential we leverage this success into broader economic opportunities."

442.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
442.text: "Golcondists, eh? Well, there's no pleasing them."

443.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
443.text: "I do gather that we Sords are not always welcome among the Rizian nobility. I hope our tourists haven't been too much of a shock to the system."

444.speaker: Player_Romus
444.text: "Whatever discomfort my relatives are feeling now is inconsequential compared to the long-term benefits of opening Valenqiris up to the world."

445.speaker: Player_Romus
445.text: "I confess I have been somewhat worried about the resort's impact on the local community."

446.speaker: Elena Werner
446.text: "A toast to the potential of our collaboration."

447.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
447.text: "Your Majesty, in my time, I've seen many a potential partnership fall through. I'm eager for this one to come to fruition."

451.speaker: Vina Toras
451.text: "It's encouraging to see such enthusiasm. Let's hope this spirit of collaboration guides us through the discussions ahead."

452.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
452.text: "Her Highness is not only here as the princess, Mr. President. She sits on His Majesty's royal council as well."

453.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
453.text: "I've done business all around the world, and I'll tell you, you won't find any better opportunities than right here."

475.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
475.text: "As you're already aware, a key aspect of these reforms is the further privatization of crucial sectors, including energy. Gasom is at the forefront of this transformation, and it's poised to play a central role in our recovery."

479.speaker: Elena Werner
479.text: "Any additional influx of economic activity is better than none, Mr. Esquibel."

480.speaker: Player_Romus
480.text: "Nonsense, Mr. Alphonso. Your people should feel free to make themselves at home in Rizia."

481.speaker: Player_Romus
481.text: "Please don't take it personally. The inhabitants of Valenqiris are slow to warm up to foreign visitors, but they'll come around."

482.speaker: Player_Romus
482.text: "It's about shaping a new economic era, where Rizia and Sordland both play pivotal roles on the global stage."

483.speaker: Player_Romus
483.text: "Agreed. But in this pursuit of international influence, we must be careful not to lose track of our own national interests."

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "We should prioritize economic prudence over global ambition."

485.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
485.text: "I just might take you up on that. I haven't been to the resort yet myself."

486.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
486.text: "Collateral is inevitable in the pursuit of progress, Your Majesty. We need to focus on the big picture — economic growth and development. That's the priority."

487.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
487.text: "You're speaking my language. National objectives, global positioning --that's where the real play is."

489.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
489.text: "Here's to the start of what could be a landmark deal."

491.speaker: Player_Romus
491.text: "This meeting is an opportunity for bold diplomatic action."

492.speaker: Player_Romus
492.text: "Concrete proposals and clear benefits for the kingdom are essential for my commitment."

493.speaker: Player_Romus
493.text: "Agreements must ensure they align with Rizia's long-term interests and stability above all."

494.speaker: Player_Romus
494.text: "I welcome new partnerships but urge us to anchor our discussions in reality."

498.speaker: Vina Toras
498.text: "As we consider this bond deal, it's important to assess its potential impact on our treasury."

514.speaker: Elena Werner
514.text: "A critical approach to our energy policies could help balance independence with efficient resource management."

515.speaker: Elena Werner
515.text: "Rizia's conservative fiscal measures have secured economic stability in the past, particularly in managing our international trade relations."

516.speaker: Vina Toras
516.text: "Mr. President, how can we ensure that the funds from this bond agreement are allocated in a way that benefits both our economy and our citizens?"

517.speaker: Vina Toras
517.text: "Mr. President, may I ask what safeguards you have in place to protect Rizia from international market fluctuations?"

518.speaker: Vina Toras
518.text: "Regarding the bond deal, how do we balance the immediate economic gains with our long-term fiscal responsibilities?"

519.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
519.text: "Princess Vina raises a key point. We need to thoroughly evaluate how this deal could affect our long-term fiscal health."

520.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
520.text: "A balance between immediate returns and long-term fiscal health is essential. We must approach this bond deal with a comprehensive fiscal strategy."

521.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
521.text: "In Sordland, our bond offerings are structured to support economic growth while maintaining fiscal responsibility."

522.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
522.text: "Excellent question, Your Highness. We anticipate that the bond proceeds will be channeled into pivotal economic sectors, providing mutual benefits to both our nations."

523.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
523.text: "A great question, Your Highness. Sordland's bond proposal includes measures to mitigate such fluctuations, ensuring a stable return on your investment."

524.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
524.text: "This bond deal is designed to strengthen Sordland's economy in a way that's sustainable and beneficial for all parties involved."

525.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
525.text: "Our approach to economic growth has always been about practicality and stability, as seen in our careful management of Rizian Royal Gold."

526.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
526.text: "Your practical approach is admirable. In Sordland, we're also striving for economic pragmatism, but with a push towards more aggressive market reforms to stimulate growth."

527.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
527.text: "Our recent advancements in natural gas extraction demonstrate the monarchy's commitment to economic prosperity."

528.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
528.text: "Sordland, too, is ambitious, but our focus is more on diversifying into sectors like technology and infrastructure."

529.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
529.text: "Ambition is the engine of progress, and we're channeling our ambitions into sweeping economic reforms. In time, Sordland will transform into a regional powerhouse."

530.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
530.text: "We have a cautious approach, ensuring our actions align with the long-term interests of the kingdom."

531.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
531.text: "While skepticism is healthy, at times it requires balancing with action. In Sordland, we're learning to blend caution with decisive moves to stay ahead economically."

532.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
532.text: "I find that bold reforms, despite initial doubts, pave the way for significant advancement."

533.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
533.text: "In our kingdom, conservatism isn't just a policy; it's a tradition. Our conservative approach has underpinned our success, as seen in our strong social services and stable economy."

534.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
534.text: "Embracing change is key to navigating the modern economic landscape."

535.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
535.text: "You need a certain degree of progressive thinking which is essential to adapt and thrive in today's global economy."

536.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
536.text: "Exactly. Which brings us back to our bond purchase proposition."

537.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
537.text: "I agree, caution is important. We've made sure to factor that into our bond purchase proposition."

538.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
538.text: "The deal we're proposing today is nothing if not prudent, Your Majesty."

539.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
539.text: "Gasom's share sales and liberal policies could be game-changers. We need to gauge how these shifts will affect the return on our bonds."

540.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
540.text: "Gasom's push to raise funds from the global market is likely to have a significant impact. But yes, it's not without its risks."

541.speaker: Elena Werner
541.text: "An interesting proposition. We must carefully analyze how it aligns with Rizia's energy security strategy."

549.speaker: Gus Manger (R)

887.speaker: Player_Romus
887.text: "We have the money. We can do both."

888.speaker: Player_Romus
888.text: "You have a point. Perhaps the money would be better spent at home."

889.speaker: Player_Romus
889.text: "This is about more than the returns alone. You're neglecting the benefits that increasing our global footprint will bring."

890.speaker: Player_Romus
890.text: "Wise words, Elena. I'm glad I brought you along."

891.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
891.text: "You're right about that. If you look at the big picture, you can't afford *not* to invest."

892.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
892.text: "Ms. Werner, you can bet that if our roles were reversed and Sordland had Rizia's treasury capabilities, we'd be all over this deal and then some."

893.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
893.text: "Close yourself off to the world for too long, and you won't have much money left to spend."

894.speaker: Elena Werner
894.text: "I'm just doing my job, Your Majesty."

895.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
895.text: "I'm afraid you know the answer. This is a now-or-never proposition."

896.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
896.text: "Besides, invest any later and you wouldn't be getting in on the ground floor."

897.speaker: Player_Romus
897.text: "We shouldn't have to spend any money to get Zille back. It's ours."

898.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
898.text: "Diplomacy can be expensive. Mr. Esquibel is right about that."

899.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
899.text: "But once you're a big enough player on the global market, other countries will be lining up to do you favors. Not the other way around."

900.speaker: Player_Romus
900.text: "It's a tight spot we're in. But I'm confident that expanding Rizia's international partnerships will help us get out of it."

902.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
902.text: "If Rizia and Sordland strengthen our bond, Wehlen will feel the squeeze. Quite literally."

906.speaker: Player_Romus
906.text: "It is a sign from the Lord. We shall pursue this deal."

910.speaker: Player_Romus
910.text: "It is a sign from the Lord. We must not pursue this deal."

911.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
911.text: "I do apologize. This meal was supposed to give you a taste of the real Sordland, not some hoity-toity millionaire's idea of it."

912.speaker: Player_Romus
912.text: "I think it looks delicious, Mr. Manger."

913.speaker: Narrator
913.text: Alphonso made a frantic cutting-off motion. Gus stopped himself.

914.speaker: Player_Romus
914.text: "It's not your fault. Everyone assumes we royals want steak and caviar all the time, but truthfully, I'd kill for a giant bowl of stew."

915.speaker: Player_Romus
915.text: "Sounds like you need to take me out to dinner sometime, Gus."

916.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
916.text: "Oh, it certainly is. But it's nothing a Bergian grandmother would recognize."

918.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
918.text: "Your Majesty, with the amount of money you've just promised to invest, I will not only take you out to dinner."

921.speaker: Narrator
921.text: Gus put his fork down with a frustrated groan.

922.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
922.text: "I think this is supposed to be Svabli, Your Majesty. A Holsord specialty. Though it's not usually this... flowery."

924.speaker: Player_Romus
924.text: "You say that as though you aren't a millionaire yourself."

925.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
925.text: "I'm not. At least, not on paper."

929.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
929.text: "Anytime. After your kingdom's investment, I owe you one."

930.speaker: Narrator
930.text: Laurento reached under the table and pulled out a bottle.

931.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
931.text: "This dish would go wonderfully with a sip of Romus the Red. A preview of the new Cantuavo vintage before it hits the Sordish market."

935.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
935.text: "This dish would go wonderfully with a sip of Romus the Red. The new Cantuavo vintage, released just recently."

936.speaker: Narrator
936.text: He poured glasses for Alphonso and his minister. Both men gave murmurs of appreciation.

937.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
937.text: "I wish that butler of yours was here to tell us more about this wine. Give him my regards when you see him?"

941.speaker: Narrator
941.text: I tried to reply as nonchalantly as possible.

942.speaker: Player_Romus
942.text: "I will if I remember. He and I are both very busy."

943.speaker: Player_Romus
943.text: "Yes, I'll give it to him. Your greeting, I mean."

944.speaker: Player_Romus
944.text: "He'll be honored to know the President of Sordland still remembers him."

945.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
945.text: "I saw pictures from the launch event in the paper. Man to man... if our Valken Kruger looked like your war councilor, I'd be going to a lot more general staff meetings."
945.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == false)

949.speaker: Narrator
949.text: I tried to reply as nonchalantly as possible.

953.speaker: Player_Romus
953.text: "You're confirming every vulgar stereotype we Rizians have of Sordland, Mr. Manger."

954.speaker: Player_Romus
954.text: "You think she's good-looking? I hadn't noticed."

955.speaker: Player_Romus
955.text: "Ha! I'll pass the compliment along to her."

956.speaker: Player_Romus
956.text: "Duchess Azaro is a prominent noblewoman and one of my most competent advisors. Please don't reduce her to her looks."

957.speaker: Narrator
957.text: Vina turned slightly green as she looked at the bottle.
957.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == false) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true)

965.speaker: Elena Werner
965.text: "Be careful, gentlemen. Consumed in sufficient amounts, this wine has been known to act as a truth serum."
965.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Pabel_Together"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn04_WineLaunch_Drunk"] >= 3  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Decision_Turn02_SordishDeal_IncludeElena"] == true)

966.speaker: Narrator
966.text: She and Laurento shared a conspiratorial smile.

967.speaker: Narrator
967.text: Just then, the third course arrived. It appeared to be a take on Bergian zabla, with medium-rare grilled sliced beef atop a silky chickpea puree.

969.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
969.text: "My deepest apologies. It was meant as a compliment."

974.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
974.text: "I'm a married man, mind you. But that doesn't mean I've gone blind."

977.speaker: Narrator
977.text: We all drank. The kebij burned my throat as it went down.

983.speaker: Narrator
983.text: We all drank. The kebij burned my throat as it went down.

992.speaker: Narrator
992.text: The Sordish minister looked pointedly at my own glass of kebij.

993.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
993.text: "Aren't you going to try our national drink, Your Majesty?"

994.speaker: Player_Romus
994.text: "I'm sure it's delicious, but no thanks."

995.speaker: Player_Romus
995.text: "Of course! Sorry, I was distracted by all the stimulating conversation."

996.speaker: Player_Romus
996.text: "I will if you assure me no one's ever gone blind from it."

997.speaker: Narrator
997.text: I took a sip. The liquor burned my throat as it went down.

999.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
999.text: "This is from a proper distillery. We'd never serve the King of Rizia the homemade stuff."

1000.speaker: Narrator
1000.text: He gave a frown of disappointment.

1001.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
1001.text: "I was looking forward to seeing your reaction. Oh, well."

1007.speaker: Player_Romus
1007.text: "All right. I'll give it a try."

1015.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
1015.text: "I will get on my knees and personally--"
